symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of vertices in the fixed experimental network.

symbols.name: \mathbb A
symbols.def: The two exposure labels \(\mathbb A=\{1,0\}\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A generic label, with \(a=1\) denoting the focal exposure and \(a=0\) denoting the comparison exposure.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The fixed adjacency matrix on the \(n\) experimental units.

symbols.name: \nu
symbols.def: The randomization distribution chosen before outcomes are observed.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: The treatment vector drawn from \(\nu\).

symbols.name: f_i
symbols.def: The exposure mapping induced by \(G\) for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: Y_i(w)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(w\).

symbols.name: D_{i,a}
symbols.def: The indicator \(D_{i,a}=\mathbf 1\{f_i(W)=a\}\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: The vector \(D=(D_{1,1},\ldots,D_{n,1},D_{1,0},\ldots,D_{n,0})^{\top}\).

symbols.name: \pi_{i,a}
symbols.def: The known probability \(\pi_{i,a}=\mathbb E_{\nu}[D_{i,a}]\).

symbols.name: \Pi
symbols.def: The diagonal matrix whose diagonal is \((\pi_{1,1},\ldots,\pi_{n,1},\pi_{1,0},\ldots,\pi_{n,0})\).

symbols.name: \Omega
symbols.def: The known matrix \(\Omega=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu}(D)\).

symbols.name: Y_i(a)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The superpopulation law of the pair \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) used only for ex ante basis choice.

symbols.name: F_a
symbols.def: The marginal law of \(Y_i(a)\) under \(H\).

symbols.name: F_1
symbols.def: The marginal \(F_a\) at \(a=1\).

symbols.name: F_0
symbols.def: The marginal \(F_a\) at \(a=0\).

symbols.name: \Gamma(F_1,F_0)
symbols.def: The class \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)=\{H\in\mathcal P([0,1]^2):\operatorname{marg}(H)=(F_1,F_0)\}\).

symbols.name: F_a^{-1}
symbols.def: The generalized inverse of the marginal distribution function.

symbols.name: \mu_a
symbols.def: The mean \(\mu_a=\int y\,dF_a(y)\).

symbols.name: \sigma_a^2
symbols.def: The variance \(\sigma_a^2=\int(y-\mu_a)^2\,dF_a(y)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C(F_1,F_0)
symbols.def: The covariance image \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=\{\operatorname{Cov}_H(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\}\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: The scalar \(c=\operatorname{Cov}_H(Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) for \(H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\).

symbols.name: Q(c)
symbols.def: For \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the matrix \(Q(c)=\begin{bmatrix}\mu_1^2\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}+\sigma_1^2I_n&-\mu_1\mu_0\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}-cI_n\\-\mu_1\mu_0\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}-cI_n&\mu_0^2\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}+\sigma_0^2I_n\end{bmatrix}\).

symbols.name: b_1
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the focal-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: b_0
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the comparison-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The matrix \(B(b_1,b_0)=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

symbols.name: S_B
symbols.def: The matrix \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\).

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: A fixed lower bound on the normalized smallest eigenvalue of \(S_B\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_Z
symbols.def: The scale-quotiented block-separable bases for which \(S_B\) is positive definite; this is the note's ordinary-inverse projective repair, not Zhao's published unquotiented feasible domain.

symbols.name: \mathcal B_\kappa
symbols.def: The compact normalized subclass with \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)\ge\kappa\).

symbols.name: g_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the Zhao gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right]\).

symbols.name: \ell_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the residual \(\ell_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]-g_B(c)\).

symbols.name: r(B)
symbols.def: The diagnostic \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\).

symbols.name: w(B)
symbols.def: The primary loss \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\).

symbols.name: v^\star
symbols.def: The diagnostic value \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_R
symbols.def: The diagnostic correspondence \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_0
symbols.def: The correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\) on the fixed normalized regular projective class; it is not Zhao's optimizer correspondence on the published unquotiented domain.
symbols.role: zero-covariance optimizer on the fixed \(\kappa\)-regular class

symbols.name: m_a
symbols.def: The number of independent unpaired pilot outcomes observed under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: Y^{P}_{j,a}
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th independent pilot draw from \(F_a\), with no cross-arm pairing.

symbols.name: \widehat F_a
symbols.def: The empirical law \(\widehat F_a=m_a^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_a}\delta_{Y^P_{j,a}}\).

symbols.name: \widehat r(B)
symbols.def: The diagnostic obtained by substituting empirical marginal moments and endpoints into \(r(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat v
symbols.def: The diagnostic value \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_R
symbols.def: The diagnostic set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: The requested numerical optimality gap.

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
symbols.def: An exact rational or real-algebraic encoding, or certified inclusion-oracle encoding with effective refinement moduli and exact feasibility decisions, of the known design matrices, both endpoint moment matrices, endpoint covariances, regularity threshold, and tolerance.

symbols.name: h_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The maximum projective-chart diameter of a box retained at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: \xi
symbols.def: The instance \(\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) with \(G\) and the exposure maps held fixed.

symbols.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
symbols.def: The relatively topologized class of instances satisfying the named predicates ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility.

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: The causal contrast \(\tau=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}\).

symbols.name: h(c)
symbols.def: For \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).

symbols.name: v_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

symbols.name: B_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: An exactly feasible basis used to certify an upper bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

symbols.name: L_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational lower bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obtained from outward-rounded lower bounds over all retained feasible boxes.

symbols.name: U_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational upper bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) certified by an exactly feasible incumbent and outward rounding.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_\varepsilon
symbols.def: The union of unpruned quotient-chart boxes, required to contain \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

symbols.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A checkable record of the chart cover, feasible incumbent, minimization bounds, retained outer boxes, exact infeasibility or lower-bound pruning records, and mesh.

symbols.name: \Delta(\xi)
symbols.def: The gap \(\Delta(\xi)=\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_\xi(B_0)-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\).

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A positive certified lower bound on \(\Delta(\xi)\).

symbols.name: \eta
symbols.def: A uniform positive lower bound on normalized nondegeneracy above \(\kappa\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).

symbols.name: \widehat w(B)
symbols.def: The endpoint residual criterion obtained by substituting the empirical marginal moments and Frechet covariance endpoints into \(w(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The value \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

assumptions.condition: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
The \(n\) pairs \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) have joint law \(H^{\otimes n}\).

standard.name: Independent and identically distributed potential-outcome pairs, Zhao Assumption 3\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 22

assumptions.condition: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
The ordered pair of marginals of \(H\) equals \((F_1,F_0)\).
The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).

standard.name: Sharp Fréchet covariance range, Aronow--Green--Lee Lemma 1

assumptions.condition: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).

standard.name: Independent product coupling with zero covariance
Supplied-basis control-variate nondegeneracy, Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).

novel.justification: Independent rescaling of either basis column leaves Zhao's control-variate span and gain unchanged, so this condition selects compact representatives without restricting implementable estimators.

standard.name: Supplied-basis nondegeneracy, fixed-threshold variant of Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: There exist vectors \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\}\ge\kappa\) for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

novel.justification: This is a verifiable design-side condition: for a fixed network, exposure maps, and known randomization, the matrix \(\Omega\) is known before outcomes are observed, so nonemptiness of the normalized \(\kappa\)-regular projective class can be certified as part of design preparation. Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) regulates a supplied basis and does not assert existence of such a normalized feasible basis.

assumptions.condition: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).

novel.justification: Separate exposure-specific historical samples are available in insurance and public-health deployments even when privacy or record linkage prevents cross-arm pairing; independence from the later randomized assignment is ensured by collecting or freezing those archives before randomization. Mikhaeil and Green inform consistency of empirical marginal endpoints, not this product sampling law.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_Z
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.

definitions.name: h(c),g_B(c),\ell_B(c)
definitions.construction: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).

definitions.name: r(B),w(B),v^\star,v_{\mathrm{mm}}
definitions.construction: Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary maximin-gain diagnostics.  The primary robust loss and minimax value are \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

definitions.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}},\mathcal A_R,\mathcal A_0
definitions.construction: On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), retain \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) as the secondary maximin-gain correspondence, define the primary minimax-residual correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\), and define the ordinarily typed zero-covariance surrogate correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
definitions.construction: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.

definitions.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
definitions.construction: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).  The exactly feasible incumbent may be represented by exact rational or real-algebraic coordinates, or by a certified inclusion-oracle name whose every requested precision terminates.  For the latter representation, exact feasibility is certified by nested closed quotient-chart boxes, each meeting \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), whose diameters tend to zero and whose intersection is the singleton \(\{B_{\varepsilon}\}\).  The checker requires \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon\); it never accepts deletion of a box meeting the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary without an exact infeasibility certificate or a valid objective lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound.

definitions.name: projective interval branch-and-bound procedure
definitions.construction: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

definitions.name: \widehat w,\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}},\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
definitions.construction: Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\); substitute them into \(Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\), \(h(c)\), \(g_B(c)\), and \(\ell_B(c)\).  Retain the resulting \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\) only as secondary diagnostics.  Define \(\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\}\), \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak X_\kappa=\{\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0):\operatorname{ass{:}exposure\mbox{-}positivity}(\xi)\wedge\operatorname{ass{:}kappa\mbox{-}feasibility}(\xi)\wedge F_1,F_0\in\mathcal P([0,1])\}\) is carved by the single named positivity and feasibility predicates, with the relative topology inherited from total variation on the finite assignment simplex and the Wasserstein metric on each bounded marginal.

definitions.name: \Delta(\xi)
definitions.construction: \(\Delta(\xi)=\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_0)-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\).  Since every member of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\) has loss \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), the second term equals \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\).

definitions.name: finite lawful minimax separation handle
definitions.construction: Start from a three-vertex network under independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/3\), enumerate the mutually exclusive exposure truth tables exactly, derive exact \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), use Bernoulli \(1/2\) pilot marginals, and analyze simultaneously the full minimax-residual and zero-covariance-surrogate correspondences.  The instance-specific certificate consists of exact optimizer equality sets, a rational lower bound \(\delta>0\) on \(\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}\), and a rational optimizer-wide regularity slack \(\eta>0\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).  This finite lawful separation handle is distinct from, and does not assert, generic finite-\(\varepsilon\) termination of the moment-complete projective interval branch-and-bound procedure.

statements.statement: Under ass:known-exposure, ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, and ass:iid-potential-pairs, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has affine functions \(c\mapsto g_B(c)\) and \(c\mapsto\ell_B(c)\) on the imported feasible domain \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\). Consequently, \(\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\), with both extrema attained. The product coupling gives \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), so \(g_B(0)\) is an ordinarily typed feasible-covariance gain. If \(c_L<0<c_U\), \(g_B(0)=\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})\) if and only if the affine slope of \(g_B\) is zero.
statements.justification: The theorem imports the published Fréchet range and proves its exact affine reduction inside Zhao's basis objective.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1, already gives the sharp covariance range. Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 4 and equation (8) on pp. 22--23, gives the covariance-dependent basis objective, and the paragraph following Theorem 4 on p. 23 substitutes the feasible zero-covariance surrogate matrix; neither source derives the affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside this projective objective.
statements.consumer: An experimenter with only two pilot marginals can evaluate the exact worst-copula gain of any proposed network basis.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By ass:exposure-positivity, every diagonal entry of \(\Pi\) is strictly positive, so \(\Pi^{-1}\) exists.  If \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), def:zhao-basis-class gives \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\), so \(S_B^{-1}\) exists.  Define
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\ I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
The construction in def:moment-matrix gives the exact identity
\[
Q(c)=Q(0)-cE.
\]
Therefore, by cyclicity and linearity of trace,
\[
g_B(c)
=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_BQ(c)\}
=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_BQ(0)\}
-c n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),
\]
which is affine in \(c\).

It remains to check the uncontrolled term rather than importing its slope.  Put \(M=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\).  For each \(i\), ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures and the definition of \(\pi_{i,a}\) imply
\[
\Omega_{i,n+i}
=\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,1},D_{i,0})
=\mathbb E_{\nu}(D_{i,1}D_{i,0})-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}
=-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}.
\]
The divisions by the two exposure probabilities are licensed by ass:exposure-positivity, and symmetry of \(\Omega\) yields
\[
\operatorname{tr}(ME)
=2\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\Omega_{i,n+i}}{\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}}
=-2n.
\]
Using def:gain-loss and \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\),
\[
h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{MQ(c)\}
=h(0)-c n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(ME)
=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Thus \(h\) is affine, and the identity \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\) in def:gain-loss proves that \(\ell_B\) is affine.  Ass:known-exposure and ass:iid-potential-pairs supply, respectively, the causal exposure interpretation and the ex ante second-moment interpretation of these matrix functionals; the displayed algebra establishes the asserted shape.

By ass:frechet-covariance-domain and def:coupling-class,
\[
\left\{\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}:H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\right\}
=[c_L,c_U].
\]
An affine real function on a compact interval attains its minimum and maximum at an endpoint.  Equality of the covariance image with the entire closed interval also says that each endpoint is attained by some coupling in \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\).  Consequently,
\[
\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
g_B\!\left(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)
=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}
\]
and
\[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\ell_B\!\left(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)
=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\},
\]
with both extrema attained.

By ass:product-coupling-zero, \(F_1\otimes F_0\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\) has covariance zero.  Ass:frechet-covariance-domain therefore gives \(0\in[c_L,c_U]\), equivalently \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), and \(g_B(0)\) is an ordinarily typed feasible-covariance gain.

Finally, write \(g_B(c)=\alpha_B+\beta_Bc\).  If \(\beta_B=0\), then \(g_B\) is constant and its value at zero equals its infimum over the coupling class.  Conversely, suppose \(c_L<0<c_U\).  If \(\beta_B>0\), then
\[
g_B(c_L)=g_B(0)+\beta_Bc_L<g_B(0),
\]
whereas if \(\beta_B<0\), then
\[
g_B(c_U)=g_B(0)+\beta_Bc_U<g_B(0).
\]
Thus \(g_B(0)\) equals the worst-coupling gain if and only if \(\beta_B=0\). \(\square\)

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa>0\), the quotient \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact and satisfies \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  Conversely, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has normalized representatives belonging to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) for some basis-dependent \(\kappa>0\), so \(\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z\).  Here \(\mathcal B_Z\) is the nondegenerate ordinary-inverse projective repair of the block-diagonal Zhao domain: the union statement covers every nonsingular implementable Zhao-type basis through a basis-dependent threshold, but it neither identifies any fixed \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) with the published class nor covers singular or pseudoinverse bases.
statements.justification: The proposition states exactly what the computational regularity restriction loses and recovers.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21, imposes boundedness and \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\lambda_\Omega n\) on a supplied basis, but does not establish existence of a normalized feasible basis or construct a compact projective exhaustion for global optimization.
statements.consumer: Certified solvers can report the regularity threshold alongside the basis instead of presenting an undocumented numerical trim.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
K_\kappa=
\left\{(b_1,b_0):
\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
\ \lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}B(b_1,b_0)^{\top}\Omega B(b_1,b_0)\right)\ge\kappa
\right\}.
\]
The product of the two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres is compact.  The map
\[
(b_1,b_0)\longmapsto n^{-1}B(b_1,b_0)^{\top}\Omega B(b_1,b_0)
\]
is continuous, as is the smallest-eigenvalue map on symmetric matrices.  Hence \(K_\kappa\) is closed in a compact set and is compact, including when it is empty.  Independent changes of sign of \(b_1\) and \(b_0\) preserve every defining condition and represent the residual projective identifications after normalization.  The quotient map is continuous, so its image \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact.

If \([B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), then
\[
\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa>0.
\]
Thus \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\) is positive definite, and def:zhao-basis-class gives \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).

Conversely, take \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\), represented by the block-separable matrix \(B=B(b_1,b_0)\).  Positive definiteness of \(S_B\) forces \(b_1\ne0\) and \(b_0\ne0\).  Define
\[
d_a=\frac{\sqrt n}{\lVert b_a\rVert_2},
\qquad
T=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_0),
\qquad
\widetilde B=BT.
\]
Then \(\widetilde B\) is a normalized representative of the same projective class, and congruence gives
\[
S_{\widetilde B}=T^{\top}S_BT=TS_BT\succ0.
\]
Consequently
\[
\rho_B=\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_{\widetilde B})>0.
\]
For example, with \(\kappa_B=\rho_B/2\), the representative \(\widetilde B\) belongs to \(\mathcal B_{\kappa_B}\).  Hence every element of \(\mathcal B_Z\) belongs to at least one \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), while the reverse inclusion was already proved, so
\[
\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z.
\]
The argument begins with \(S_B\succ0\) and uses a basis-dependent threshold.  It therefore exhausts precisely the nondegenerate ordinary-inverse projective repair in def:zhao-basis-class; it neither equates any fixed \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) with Zhao's unquotiented block-diagonal domain nor reaches singular or pseudoinverse bases. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi_0)>0\) and there is \(\eta>0\) such that \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\}\ge\eta\), then there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) of \(\xi_0\) such that \(\Delta(\xi)>0\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\).
statements.justification: Persistence upgrades any exact finite witness from a curiosity to a nondegenerate region of lawful experiments.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals gives continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences, while GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust gives a general dependence-robust decision template; neither proves strict robust-basis dominance for Zhao's optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: Any certified output of oeq:separated-lawful-witness with \(\delta>0\) and optimizer-wide slack \(\eta>0\) activates this theorem and yields a relative-open region on which every robust optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance-surrogate optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The hypotheses are those of lem:dominance-gap-lower-semicontinuity, and \(\Delta(\xi_0)>0\).  If no relative-open neighborhood of \(\xi_0\) had positive gap throughout, metrizability of the total-variation--Wasserstein product topology would provide a sequence \(\xi_j\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) such that \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) and \(\Delta(\xi_j)\le0\) for every \(j\).  The lemma would then imply
\[
0\ge\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)
\ge\Delta(\xi_0)>0,
\]
a contradiction.  Therefore there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) of \(\xi_0\) such that \(\Delta(\xi)>0\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\). \(\square\)

statements.statement: Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, so \(\mathcal B_\kappa\neq\varnothing\).  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, as \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\to0\) almost surely, \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}\to v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely, and every subsequential limit of \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely.  Equivalently, \(\limsup_{m_1,m_0\to\infty}\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely in the projective quotient.
statements.justification: The set-valued conclusion is the strongest valid generic guarantee when projective symmetries or endpoint ties create multiple optimizers.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance and MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment prove scalar endpoint consistency; Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 3, concerns estimated-coefficient consistency and asymptotics but does not establish uniform global basis-objective or argmax-correspondence consistency.
statements.consumer: An independent historical or external pilot can select a robust network basis without pretending that its two marginal samples identify a cross-world copula.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Work with normalized representatives of the projective classes in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  By prop:kappa-exhaustion and ass:kappa-feasibility, the quotient is a nonempty compact metrizable space.  The two columns of every normalized representative have disjoint block supports and squared Euclidean norm \(n\), while the defining \(\kappa\)-regularity inequality gives
\[
 \lVert B\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=\sqrt n,
 \qquad
 \lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le (n\kappa)^{-1}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  The matrices \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\) are fixed because the network, exposure maps, and assignment law are fixed.

Write \(q_a=F_a^{-1}\) and \(\widehat q_a=\widehat F_a^{-1}\).  We first establish convergence of every pilot ingredient.  If \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are independent, centered, and bounded in absolute value by one, expansion of the fourth moment and independence give
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^m X_j\right)^4
 =\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^4
   +6\sum_{1\le i<j\le m}\mathbb E X_i^2\,\mathbb E X_j^2
 \le 3m^2.
 \tag{2}
\]
For every \(t>0\), Markov's inequality therefore bounds the probability that the empirical average has absolute value greater than \(t\) by \(3/(m^2t^4)\).  Summability and the Borel--Cantelli lemma prove the bounded strong law.  Apply this argument in each pilot arm to the outcomes, their squares, and, simultaneously over rational \(x\), the indicators \(\mathbf 1\{Y^P_{j,a}\le x\}\).  Monotonicity of distribution functions then gives \(\widehat F_a(x)\to F_a(x)\) at every continuity point of \(F_a\).  The generalized-inverse squeeze consequently gives \(\widehat q_a(u)\to q_a(u)\) at every continuity point of \(q_a\).  Since a monotone function has at most countably many discontinuities and all these quantiles lie in \([0,1]\), dominated convergence yields
\[
 \lVert\widehat q_a-q_a\rVert_{L^1(0,1)}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \widehat\mu_a\longrightarrow\mu_a,
 \qquad
 \widehat\sigma_a^2\longrightarrow\sigma_a^2
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The two armwise probability-one events may be intersected because there are only two arms; ass:unpaired-pilot supplies the required i.i.d. sequences.  Independence from \(W\) is compatible with, and keeps separate, the pilot probability-one event and the later design randomization.

Because all quantiles are bounded by one,
\[
 \left|
  \int_0^1\widehat q_1(u)\widehat q_0(u)\,du
  -\int_0^1q_1(u)q_0(u)\,du
 \right|
 \le
 \lVert\widehat q_1-q_1\rVert_1
 +\lVert\widehat q_0-q_0\rVert_1.
 \tag{4}
\]
The same bound holds with the second quantile evaluated at \(1-u\).  Thus the quantile definitions of the Fr\'echet endpoints imply
\[
 \widehat c_L\longrightarrow c_L,
 \qquad
 \widehat c_U\longrightarrow c_U
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Assumption ass:frechet-covariance-domain ensures that these are exactly the two sharp feasible-covariance endpoints used by the population worst-copula criterion.  For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), set \(Q_e=Q(c_e)\), and let \(\widehat Q_e\) denote the matrix obtained from the corresponding empirical moments and empirical endpoint.  Equations (3)--(5) and the finite-dimensional formula in def:moment-matrix imply
\[
 \rho_m:=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
 \lVert\widehat Q_e-Q_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{almost surely as }m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty.
 \tag{6}
\]

Put \(C_\nu=\lVert\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\) and \(A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\).  For a \(d\)-dimensional square matrix \(M\), the elementary singular-value inequality \(|\operatorname{tr}(M)|\le d\lVert M\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), together with def:gain-loss and (1), gives uniformly over \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\)
\[
 \max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
 |\widehat g_B(\widehat c_e)-g_B(c_e)|
 \le \frac{2C_\nu^2}{n^2\kappa}\rho_m,
 \tag{7}
\]
because the trace in the gain is two-dimensional.  The analogous \(2n\)-dimensional trace bound gives
\[
 \max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
 |\widehat h(\widehat c_e)-h(c_e)|
 \le \frac{2}{n}\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\rho_m.
 \tag{8}
\]
Subtracting the gain from the uncontrolled variance, as prescribed by def:gain-loss, bounds the two endpoint residual errors by the sum of the right sides of (7) and (8), uniformly in \(B\).  The maximum of two real coordinates is one-Lipschitz for the sup norm.  Hence
\[
 \delta_m:=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}
 |\widehat w(B)-w(B)|longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
 \tag{9}
\]

For each endpoint, the loss is continuous on \(\mathcal B_\kappa\): all matrix operations are continuous, and (1) keeps inversion uniformly away from singularity.  Therefore \(w\) and \(\widehat w\) are continuous and attain minima on the nonempty compact quotient.  The elementary inequality comparing minima of two uniformly close functions gives
\[
 |\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}-v_{\mathrm{mm}}|
 \le\delta_m\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
 \tag{10}
\]

It remains to prove the outer correspondence statement.  Take any sequence \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and any convergent subsequence \(B_{m_j}\to B_\infty\); compactness ensures that subsequences of this kind exist.  For an arbitrary \(B^\star\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\), empirical optimality and (9) imply
\[
 w(B_{m_j})
 \le \widehat w(B_{m_j})+\delta_{m_j}
 \le \widehat w(B^\star)+\delta_{m_j}
 \le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\delta_{m_j}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Continuity of \(w\), (9), and the defining inequality \(w\ge v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) now yield \(w(B_\infty)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  Thus \(B_\infty\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\), which is exactly
\[
 \limsup_{m_1,m_0\to\infty}\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
 \subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}
\]
in the projective quotient. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{B^\star\}\) in the projective quotient, \(B^\star\) is isolated by a positive loss gap outside every neighborhood, and exactly one of \(c_L,c_U\) attains \(w(B^\star)\), then every measurable selection \(\widehat B\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) converges almost surely to \(B^\star\).  Without the singleton condition, there exist bounded two-marginal instances satisfying the maintained assumptions for which the outer-set conclusion of thm:plugin-correspondence holds but some measurable plug-in selections fail to converge to a point.
statements.justification: This proposition draws the exact line between defensible set consistency and unjustified point consistency.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals implies upper hemicontinuity for optimizer sets but does not give this pilot-based quotient-space selection result or its tie counterexample.
statements.consumer: Applied reporting can retain all empirically indistinguishable robust bases unless an isolated unique saddle is actually verified.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Work on the probability-one event on which thm:plugin-correspondence holds, and let \(U\) be any neighborhood of \(B^\star\).  The assumed isolation by a positive loss gap says
\[
 \gamma_U:=inf_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\setminus U}w(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}>0.
 \tag{1}
\]
Let \(\delta_m=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\), so thm:plugin-correspondence gives \(\delta_m\to0\).  If \(2\delta_m<\gamma_U\), every \(B\notin U\) satisfies
\[
 \widehat w(B)
 \ge w(B)-\delta_m
 \ge v_{\mathrm{mm}}+\gamma_U-\delta_m
 >v_{\mathrm{mm}}+\delta_m
 \ge\widehat w(B^\star).
 \tag{2}
\]
Consequently \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\subset U\) eventually.  Since \(U\) was arbitrary, every measurable selection \(\widehat B\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) converges almost surely to \(B^\star\).  The hypothesis that exactly one endpoint is active labels the limiting saddle unambiguously; once singleton isolation is assumed, it is not additionally needed for convergence of the basis coordinate.

We next construct the claimed failure of point convergence when the singleton condition is absent.  Let \(n=3\), take \(f_i(w)=w_i\), and let the coordinates of \(W\) be independent Bernoulli random variables with success probability \(1/2\).  The two exposure events are mutually exclusive, every exposure probability equals \(1/2\), and direct calculation gives
\[
 \Pi=\frac12 I_6,
 \qquad
 \Omega=\frac14
 \begin{bmatrix}
 I_3&-I_3\\
 -I_3&I_3
 \end{bmatrix}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Let \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\), take \(H=\delta_{(0,0)}\), and use the corresponding two unpaired pilot sequences.  The outcomes are bounded and the pilot samples are i.i.d., unpaired, and independent of the later assignment.  Moreover,
\[
 \mu_1=\mu_0=\sigma_1^2=\sigma_0^2=c_L=c_U=0,
 \qquad
 Q(0)=0.
 \tag{4}
\]
Choose \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(e_j\) denoting the coordinate vectors of \(\mathbb R^3\), define
\[
 B^{(2)}=B(\sqrt3e_1,\sqrt3e_2),
 \qquad
 B^{(3)}=B(\sqrt3e_1,\sqrt3e_3).
\]
For \(j\in\{2,3\}\), equation (3) and the orthogonality of the selected coordinates give
\[
 S_{B^{(j)}}=\frac34 I_2,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}\!\left(3^{-1}S_{B^{(j)}}\right)=\frac14>\kappa.
 \tag{5}
\]
Thus ass:kappa-feasibility holds, and the two displayed matrices determine distinct feasible projective points.  By (4), however, def:gain-loss gives \(h(0)=g_B(0)=\ell_B(0)=w(B)=0\) for every feasible \(B\).  Every pilot observation is identically zero, so the same equalities hold for the plug-in quantities at every pilot size.  Therefore
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
 =\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}
 =\mathcal B_\kappa
 \quad\text{at every pilot size}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Along the diagonal sequence \(m_1=m_0=m\), select \(B^{(2)}\) for even \(m\) and \(B^{(3)}\) for odd \(m\).  This deterministic rule is a measurable plug-in selection and has two distinct subsequential limits.  At the same time, (6) makes the outer-set inclusion of thm:plugin-correspondence exact.  Hence generic outer consistency does not imply point convergence without the singleton condition. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/100\), the marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\) produce the same moment-incomplete tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their endpoint moment matrices differ and their minimax residual values are, respectively,
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]
Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \((\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon)\) can always return rational bounds
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus endpoint moment matrices such as \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), or equivalent marginal moments, are necessary inputs for the proposed certification problem.  This obstruction makes no claim that the corrected moment-complete branch-and-bound solver terminates at every positive tolerance.
statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Proof.}
Write \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and
\[
K=\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Because \(f_i(W)=W_i\), the two exposure indicators are \(D_{i,1}=W_i\) and \(D_{i,0}=1-W_i\).  They are mutually exclusive on every assignment.  Independence and \(\operatorname{Var}_{\nu}(W_i)=1/4\) therefore give, entry by entry,
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,
\qquad
\Omega=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu}(D)=\tfrac14K.
\]
Exposure positivity holds because every diagonal entry of \(\Pi\) is \(1/2\), so \(\Pi^{-1}=2I_6\) exists.

We next verify that the normalized regular basis class is nonempty and that the witness is away from its boundary.  Set
\[
b_1=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\end{bmatrix}^{\top},
\qquad
b_0=\sqrt{\tfrac32}\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&0\end{bmatrix}^{\top}.
\]
Then \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=3\) and \(b_1^{\top}b_0=0\).  For the associated block-separable basis,
\[
S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B
=\tfrac14
\begin{bmatrix}
3&-b_1^{\top}b_0\\
-b_0^{\top}b_1&3
\end{bmatrix}
=\tfrac34I_2.
\]
Hence \(\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=1/4>1/8=\kappa\).  This proves feasibility and the rank condition rather than assuming them; in particular, every inverse used below exists for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\).

For \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\), all marginal means and variances vanish.  Both quantile products vanish, so \(c_L=c_U=0\), and the moment-matrix definition gives \(Q(0)=0\).  Therefore \(\ell_B(0)=0\) for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), whence
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0.
\]

Now take \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\).  Both marginals are supported on \([0,1]\).  Since the comparison potential outcome is constant, every coupling has covariance zero; equivalently, direct evaluation of both quantile integrals gives \(c_L=c_U=0\).  Here
\[
\mu_1=\tfrac12,
\quad \sigma_1^2=\tfrac14,
\quad \mu_0=\sigma_0^2=0,
\quad
Q(0)=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A=\tfrac14(I_3+J_3).
\]
Thus the two marginal pairs have the same displayed moment-incomplete tuple, although their endpoint moment matrices are different.

It remains to calculate the second minimax residual exactly.  Let \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) be arbitrary, write \(x=b_1\), \(y=b_0\), and put \(C=[x,-y]\).  Projective normalization gives \(\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3\).  Moreover, \(\kappa\)-regularity makes \(S_B\) positive definite, so \(C\) has rank two.  Direct block multiplication, using \(\Pi^{-1}=2I_6\) and \(\Omega=K/4\), yields
\[
S_B=\tfrac14C^{\top}C,
\qquad
B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(0)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B
=\tfrac14C^{\top}AC.
\]
Consequently, if
\[
P_C=C(C^{\top}C)^{-1}C^{\top}
\]
denotes the rank-two orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{col}(C)\), cyclicity of trace gives
\[
g_B(0)
=\tfrac19\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(C^{\top}C)^{-1}C^{\top}AC\right]
=\tfrac19\operatorname{tr}(P_CA).
\]
The basis-free term in the residual is
\[
h(0)
:=\tfrac19\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(0)\right]
=\tfrac19\operatorname{tr}(A)
=\tfrac16.
\]
Let \(u=3^{-1/2}\mathbf 1\).  Since \(J_3=3uu^{\top}\),
\[
A=\tfrac14I_3+\tfrac34uu^{\top}.
\]
Because \(P_C\) is an orthogonal projector of rank two,
\[
\operatorname{tr}(P_CA)
=\tfrac14\operatorname{tr}(P_C)+\tfrac34u^{\top}P_Cu
=\tfrac12+\tfrac34\lVert P_Cu\rVert_2^2
\le\tfrac54.
\]
It follows for every feasible basis that
\[
\ell_B(0)=h(0)-g_B(0)
\ge\tfrac16-\tfrac19\cdot\tfrac54
=\tfrac1{36}.
\]
The previously displayed feasible choice has \(b_1=\sqrt3u\) and \(b_0\perp u\), so \(u\in\operatorname{col}(C)\), \(\lVert P_Cu\rVert_2=1\), and equality holds throughout.  Because the covariance interval is the singleton \(\{0\}\), \(w(B)=\ell_B(0)\), proving
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\tfrac1{36}.
\]

Finally, an algorithm receiving only the displayed moment-incomplete tuple must return the same \((L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon})\) on these two instances.  Validity on both would force \([L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}]\) to contain both \(0\) and \(1/36\), so
\[
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\ge\tfrac1{36}>\tfrac1{100}=\varepsilon,
\]
contradicting the required tolerance.  The contradiction concerns only omission of the endpoint moment matrices and therefore does not establish existence or finite termination of the repaired moment-complete solver.

The causal estimand remains the finite-population exposure contrast \(\tau\).  The minimax residual is an ex ante design criterion for choosing a control-variate basis; it is not an identifying formula for \(\tau\).  \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying exposure positivity and \(\kappa\)-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the candidate projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
Here \(B_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) is represented exactly, including when the feasible set has no relative interior and lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  A chart box meeting that equality boundary is never discarded as infeasible; it may be discarded only when its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound.  Consequently, along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and retained-box mesh diameters converge to zero.  This is a finite, instance-dependent termination result; it asserts neither a uniform complexity bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}

\emph{Step 1: compact feasible charts.}
Work with normalized representatives and put
\[
K_\kappa=
\left\{(b_1,b_0):
\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
\quad
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\right)\ge\kappa
\right\}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}kappa\mbox{-}feasibility}\) makes \(K_\kappa\) nonempty, and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}kappa\mbox{-}exhaustion}\) shows that its projective quotient is the nonempty compact set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  If \(b\) lies on the radius-\(\sqrt n\) sphere, then some coordinate satisfies \(\lvert b_j\rvert\ge1\), and hence \(\lvert b_j\rvert\ge n^{-1/2}\).  After the projective sign identification, that coordinate can be taken positive and recovered from the other coordinates by
\[
b_j=\left(n-\sum_{k\ne j}b_k^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
On the stated pivot region the radicand is at least \(n^{-1}\).  The finitely many pivot maps and their inverses therefore have effective uniform-continuity moduli.  Their products give the finite quotient-chart cover used by the procedure.  The exact feasibility interface decides sphere feasibility and the closed inequality defining \(K_\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.

\emph{Step 2: an effective modulus for the loss.}
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), abbreviate
\[
Q_e=Q(c_e),
\qquad
R_e=\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q_e\Pi^{-1}\Omega,
\qquad
S(B)=B^{\top}\Omega B,
\qquad
T_e(B)=B^{\top}R_eB.
\]
Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well-defined.  There are finitely many exposure probabilities, so refinement of their certified enclosures terminates with a positive rational lower bound for \(\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}\).  Exact positivity of \(\kappa\) similarly gives a positive rational lower bound for \(\kappa\).  The moment-complete input consequently supplies computable finite rational bounds
\[
M_\Omega\ge\lVert\Omega\rVert_2,
\qquad
M_e\ge\lVert R_e\rVert_2.
\]

Every normalized block matrix satisfies \(\lVert B\rVert_F=\sqrt{2n}\).  Hence, for \(d=\lVert B-C\rVert_F\), submultiplicativity and the identity
\(B^{\top}MB-C^{\top}MC=(B-C)^{\top}MB+C^{\top}M(B-C)\) give
\[
\lVert S(B)-S(C)\rVert_2\le K_Sd,
\qquad
\lVert T_e(B)-T_e(C)\rVert_2\le K_{T,e}d,
\]
where
\[
K_S=2\sqrt{2n}\,M_\Omega,
\qquad
K_{T,e}=2\sqrt{2n}\,M_e.
\]
For \(B\in K_\kappa\),
\[
S(B)\succeq n\kappa I_2,
\qquad
\lVert S(B)^{-1}\rVert_2\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\]
If \(B,C\in K_\kappa\), the resolvent identity
\[
S(B)^{-1}-S(C)^{-1}
=S(B)^{-1}\{S(C)-S(B)\}S(C)^{-1}
\]
and \(\lvert\operatorname{tr}(XY)\rvert\le2\lVert X\rVert_2\lVert Y\rVert_2\) for two-by-two matrices imply
\[
\lvert g_B(c_e)-g_C(c_e)\rvert\le L_e d,
\]
with the effective finite constant
\[
L_e=n^{-2}\left\{
\frac{2K_{T,e}}{n\kappa}
+\frac{4nM_eK_S}{(n\kappa)^2}
\right\},
\]
because \(\lVert T_e(C)\rVert_2\le2nM_e\).  The uncontrolled term \(h(c_e)\) is independent of \(B\), and the maximum map is one-Lipschitz in the sup norm.  Thus
\[
\lvert w(B)-w(C)\rvert
\le L\lVert B-C\rVert_F,
\qquad
L=\max\{L_L,L_U\}.
\]
Composition with the finitely many pivot maps yields an effective chartwise modulus \(\omega(\rho)\downarrow0\).

The same construction controls interval boxes that merely meet the feasible set.  If a box of ambient diameter \(\rho\) contains \(B\in K_\kappa\), then every \(C\) in that box obeys
\[
\lambda_{\min}\{S(C)\}
\ge n\kappa-K_S\rho.
\]
For \(K_S\rho\le n\kappa/2\), one has \(S(C)\succeq(n\kappa/2)I_2\) throughout that box.  Matrix inversion is uniformly stable there.  Outward-rounded interval evaluation of addition, multiplication, trace, inversion, the two endpoint losses, and their maximum therefore has a computable width tending to zero as the box diameter and arithmetic-enclosure widths tend to zero.  Explicitly, if \([\underline\ell_e,\overline\ell_e]\) encloses \(\ell_B(c_e)\), then
\[
\left[
\max_e\underline\ell_e,
\max_e\overline\ell_e
\right]
\]
encloses \(w(B)\), and its width tends to zero.  Interval-Hessian underestimators may improve these bounds but are not needed for convergence.

\emph{Step 3: exact feasible witness extraction, including at the boundary.}
Let \(C\) be a closed chart box for which the exact feasibility oracle answers \(C\cap K_\kappa\ne\varnothing\).  Bisect \(C\), query its finitely many children, retain the first child having nonempty intersection with \(K_\kappa\), and repeat.  This constructs nested closed boxes \(C=C_0\supseteq C_1\supseteq\cdots\) such that
\[
C_m\cap K_\kappa\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}(C_m)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Their intersection is a singleton \(\{B_C\}\).  Since \(K_\kappa\) is closed and each \(C_m\) meets \(K_\kappa\), choose \(x_m\in C_m\cap K_\kappa\); then \(x_m\to B_C\), so \(B_C\in K_\kappa\).  The finite program that performs this bisection to any requested precision, together with the effective diameter modulus and exact feasibility oracle, is a certified inclusion-oracle name for \(B_C\).  Every requested precision terminates after finitely many exact decisions.  It is therefore an exact representation of a feasible point, as expressly allowed for \(B_\varepsilon\) by the certified-output contract, and not a floating-point point whose feasibility is merely asserted.  Nothing in this construction requires strict inequality; it remains valid when all feasible points in \(C\) satisfy
\[
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\right)=\kappa.
\]

\emph{Step 4: simultaneous value and mesh guarantees.}
Fix the exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\).  Its exact positive encoding permits selection of a rational \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<\varepsilon/4\).  The effective moduli in Step 2 allow the procedure to find a finite common chart depth \(N\) and a finite arithmetic-refinement precision such that every depth-\(N\) box has chart diameter at most \(\varepsilon\), every such box meeting \(K_\kappa\) lies in the stable-inverse region, and, for each feasible box \(C\),
\[
\inf_{B\in C\cap K_\kappa}w(B)-\alpha
\le \underline w(C)
\le \inf_{B\in C\cap K_\kappa}w(B),
\]
while the exact feasible name from Step 3 has a rational outward-rounded upper bound satisfying
\[
w(B_C)\le\overline w(B_C)\le w(B_C)+\alpha.
\]
To justify the first display even though interval evaluation ranges over the whole chart box, fix any feasible point of \(C\).  Every point of \(C\) is within its diameter of that feasible point; the stable-region modulus and sufficiently fine arithmetic refinement bound the resulting downward interval overestimation by \(\alpha\).

There are finitely many depth-\(N\) boxes.  Delete those certified exactly infeasible.  Among the remaining boxes, choose the least rational upper bound \(\overline w(B_C)\); call its exact feasible inclusion-oracle name \(B_\varepsilon\) and call that bound \(U_\varepsilon\).  Continuity from Step 2 and nonempty compactness from Step 1 give a minimizer \(B^\star\in\mathcal B_\kappa\).  Let \(C^\star\) be a depth-\(N\) box containing it.  Refining \(N\), if necessary, so that the loss oscillation on every feasible box is at most \(\alpha\), gives
\[
U_\varepsilon
\le\overline w(B_{C^\star})
\le w(B_{C^\star})+\alpha
\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\alpha.
\]

Let \(L_\varepsilon\) be the minimum certified lower bound over all unpruned feasible boxes.  The box containing \(B^\star\) has lower bound at most \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  Every feasible box has true infimum at least \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\), so its lower bound is at least \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}-\alpha\).  Therefore
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}-\alpha
\le L_\varepsilon
\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le w(B_\varepsilon)
\le U_\varepsilon
\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\alpha,
\]
and hence
\[
U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon\le3\alpha<\varepsilon.
\]
All reported interval endpoints are rational because they are obtained by outward rounding.

Pruning preserves every global minimizer.  If \(\underline w(C)>U_\varepsilon\), then each feasible point in \(C\) has loss strictly greater than the loss of the feasible incumbent, so \(C\) contains no global minimizer.  Conversely, a box containing a member of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) is neither exactly infeasible nor objective-prunable, because
\[
\underline w(C)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le w(B_\varepsilon)
\le U_\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently the union \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) of the retained quotient-chart boxes contains \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\), and its maximum box diameter obeys \(h_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\).

\emph{Step 5: finite termination and certificate verification.}
The initial chart family is finite, subdivision to depth \(N\) creates only finitely many boxes, every exact feasibility query terminates under the input contract, and every requested inclusion-oracle and interval refinement terminates under the effective moduli.  Thus the procedure reaches the displayed value-gap and mesh conditions no later than the finite exhaustive refinement depth \(N\); valid earlier pruning can only reduce the work.  A box meeting the exact feasible \(\kappa\)-boundary has nonempty feasible intersection, so the exact oracle cannot label it infeasible.  Such a box is retained unless its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound, and the preceding pruning inequality shows that this rule cannot discard a minimizer.

The finite chart cover, the certified inclusion-oracle name of \(B_\varepsilon\), the rational bounds, every exact-infeasibility or objective-pruning record, and the retained boxes form \(\mathscr K_\varepsilon\).  Steps 3 and 4 establish exactly the checks required by the certified-output definition:
\[
L_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_\varepsilon)\le U_\varepsilon,
\qquad
U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon.
\]
Because the construction works for every positive \(\varepsilon\), along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) it yields \(U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon\to0\) and \(h_\varepsilon\to0\).  The depth \(N\), enclosure precision, and number of boxes may depend on the encoded instance and on \(\varepsilon\); no uniform complexity or semidefinite-program representation has been used or proved. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Let \(E_1,E_0\) be compact metric spaces.  Under weak convergence of an ordered pair of marginal probability measures, the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence is continuous in the weak topology.  Consequently, for every continuous function \(\varphi:E_1\times E_0\to\mathbb R\), the minimum and maximum of \(H\mapsto\int\varphi\,dH\) over the coupling set vary continuously with the ordered marginal pair, and the associated optimizer correspondences are upper hemicontinuous.

Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\) and both regular classes are nonempty, then
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
\le
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
=
\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
If the right-hand infimum is attained by some \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_Z\), then there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that, for every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
This value transfer concerns only the nonsingular ordinary-inverse projective class \(\mathcal B_Z\), not singular or pseudoinverse bases or Zhao's larger unquotiented domain.
statements.justification: This is the exact converse-value transfer justified by the compact projective exhaustion.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates does not introduce a normalized threshold family or prove convergence of its optimization values as the threshold vanishes.
statements.consumer: A solver can report how its fixed regularity threshold approximates the best value over the entire nonsingular ordinary-inverse projective repair.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\), the common normalization and the eigenvalue inequalities give
\[
\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}.
\]
Minimizing the same function over the larger set proves the first displayed inequality.  On each nonempty \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), compactness from prop:kappa-exhaustion and continuity of the ordinary-inverse trace formula imply that the displayed minimum is attained.

Prop:kappa-exhaustion also gives
\[
\mathcal B_Z=\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa.
\]
For an arbitrary function, the infimum over a union equals the infimum of the infima over its nonempty members.  Applying this identity to \(w\) yields
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=
\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\]

Finally, suppose \(B_Z^\star\) attains the right-hand infimum.  By prop:kappa-exhaustion there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_0}\).  For every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\), nesting gives \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), while \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  Therefore
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
\le
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
\le
w(B_Z^\star)
=
\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
\]
which proves equality throughout.  No step enlarges \(\mathcal B_Z\) beyond its nondegenerate ordinary-inverse definition. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).  Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, ass:frechet-covariance-domain, and ass:product-coupling-zero,
\[
h(c)=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.
\]
If \(c_L<c_U\), minimization of \(w(B)\) is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\): as functions of a formal endpoint-gain pair \((x_L,x_U)\), the two loss criteria are not related by a constant independent of \((x_L,x_U)\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\ I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
By def:moment-matrix,
\[
Q(c)=Q(0)-cE.
\]
The expression \(Q(0)\) is well typed because ass:product-coupling-zero gives \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\); ass:frechet-covariance-domain further identifies this feasible domain with \([c_L,c_U]\).

For each unit \(i\), ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures gives \(D_{i,1}D_{i,0}=0\) almost surely.  Therefore
\[
\Omega_{i,n+i}
=\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,1},D_{i,0})
=\mathbb E_{\nu}[D_{i,1}D_{i,0}]-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}
=-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}.
\]
Assumption ass:exposure-positivity permits division by both exposure probabilities.  Since \(A_{\mathrm{HT}}\) is symmetric and \(E\) exchanges the two exposure blocks,
\[
\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)
=2\sum_{i=1}^n(A_{\mathrm{HT}})_{i,n+i}
=2\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\Omega_{i,n+i}}{\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}}
=-2n.
\]
Linearity of trace now gives, for every feasible \(c\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
h(c)
&=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_{\mathrm{HT}}(Q(0)-cE)\}\\
&=h(0)-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)\\
&=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Using def:gain-loss and def:robust-objective, substitute this identity into
\(w(B)=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\{h(c_e)-g_B(c_e)\}\) to obtain
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{
\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),
\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)
\right\}.
\]

It remains to verify the asserted algebraic non-equivalence.  Put \(a_e=2c_e/n\).  For a formal endpoint-gain pair \(x=(x_L,x_U)\in\mathbb R^2\), define
\[
\Phi(x)=\max\{a_L-x_L,a_U-x_U\},
\qquad
\Psi(x)=\max\{-x_L,-x_U\}=-\min\{x_L,x_U\}.
\]
Up to the basis-independent constant \(h(0)\), minimization of worst residual uses \(\Phi\), whereas maximization of \(r(B)\) is equivalent to minimization of \(\Psi\).  Suppose there were a constant \(K\), independent of \(x\), such that \(\Phi(x)=\Psi(x)+K\) for all \(x\).  With \(x=(t,0)\), letting \(t\to\infty\) gives \(K=a_U\).  With \(x=(0,t)\), letting \(t\to\infty\) gives \(K=a_L\).  Hence such a constant can exist only if \(a_L=a_U\), equivalently \(c_L=c_U\).  When \(c_L<c_U\), the two formal criteria are therefore not related by a basis-independent additive constant. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility hold.  The primary minimax correspondence is nonempty and satisfies the unconditional weak worst-copula dominance certificate
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]
Strict inequality is not universal and requires a separate lawful witness.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Assumption ass:kappa-feasibility makes \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) nonempty, and Proposition prop:kappa-exhaustion makes it compact.  Assumption ass:exposure-positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  For every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), ass:kappa-regularity, as incorporated in def:kappa-basis-class, gives
\[
S_B\succeq n\kappa I_2,
\qquad
\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le (n\kappa)^{-1}.
\]
Thus inversion is continuous on the full feasible class.  Matrix multiplication and trace are continuous, so the formulas in def:gain-loss imply that \(B\mapsto g_B(0)\), \(B\mapsto\ell_B(c_L)\), and \(B\mapsto\ell_B(c_U)\) are continuous on normalized representatives.  Each formula is invariant under the independent sign changes that remain after projective normalization, and therefore descends continuously to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  The maximum of the two continuous endpoint losses is continuous, so \(B\mapsto w(B)\) is continuous as well.

By the extreme-value theorem, the minimum defining \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and the maximum defining \(\mathcal A_0\) are both attained.  Hence both correspondences are nonempty and compact.  For arbitrary \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0\), the defining minimization in def:robust-objective gives
\[
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_0).
\]
The left-hand side is constant over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  Taking the supremum over \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\), and then the infimum over \(B_0\), yields
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]

Strictness cannot follow from these assumptions.  To see this within the lawful class, fix any design satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility and take \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\).  Then \(\mu_1=\mu_0=\sigma_1^2=\sigma_0^2=0\) and \(c_L=c_U=0\), so def:moment-matrix gives \(Q(0)=0\).  Consequently def:gain-loss gives \(g_B(0)=\ell_B(0)=w(B)=0\) for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\).  Thus equality holds in the displayed certificate for this lawful instance.  Any strict inequality therefore requires a separate lawful witness. \(\square\)

Let \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) and suppose that, for some \(\eta>0\),
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}\ge\eta.
\]
For every sequence \((\xi_j)_{j\ge1}\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) converging to \(\xi_0\) in the relative topology of def:lawful-instance-class,
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)\ge\Delta(\xi_0).
\]
statements.justification: This quantitative lower-semicontinuity lemma is the reusable step that turns an exact optimizer-wide slack certificate into a uniform dominance margin.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals supplies continuity of the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence; the new step propagates that continuity through the moving regular projective feasible set and both optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: The triangle neighborhood corollary uses the lemma to preserve half of the exact rational separation margin.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(K(\xi)=\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)\), viewed inside the compact quotient of the product of the two normalized radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres.  We first establish joint continuity of the ingredients.

Because the assignment space is finite, total-variation convergence \(\nu_j\to\nu_0\) implies entrywise convergence of \(\Pi_j\) and \(\Omega_j\).  Exposure positivity at \(\xi_0\), together with finiteness of the \(2n\) diagonal entries, gives a neighborhood on which all exposure probabilities are bounded away from zero.  Hence
\[
\Pi_j^{-1}\longrightarrow\Pi_0^{-1}.
\]
Wasserstein convergence on \([0,1]\) implies weak convergence.  By lem:restricted-marginal-extrema-continuity, the minimum and maximum of
\[
H\longmapsto\int y_1y_0\,dH(y_1,y_0)
\]
over \(H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\) vary continuously with the ordered marginal pair.  Ass:frechet-covariance-domain identifies these extrema, after subtraction of \(\mu_1\mu_0\), with \(c_L\) and \(c_U\).  The first and second marginal moments also converge because \(y\) and \(y^2\) are bounded continuous functions on \([0,1]\).  It follows from def:moment-matrix that \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\) vary continuously with \(\xi\).

The map
\[
(\xi,B)\longmapsto
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega(\xi)B\right)
\tag{1}
\]
is continuous on the normalized ambient quotient, and its \(\kappa\)-superlevel graph is closed.  On that graph,
\[
\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
The finite-dimensional trace formulas in def:gain-loss, the continuity just proved, and (2) show that
\[
(\xi,B)\longmapsto g_{B,\xi}(0)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(\xi,B)\longmapsto w_\xi(B)
\tag{3}
\]
are jointly continuous on the feasible graph.  These functions are invariant under the projective sign identifications, so (3) is well defined on the quotient.

We next establish sequential upper stability of the two optimizer correspondences at \(\xi_0\).  Suppose \(B_j\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)\) and, after passage to a subsequence in the compact ambient quotient, \(B_j\to B\).  Closedness of the feasible graph gives \(B\in K(\xi_0)\).  Choose \(B^\circ\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\), which exists because ass:kappa-feasibility, prop:kappa-exhaustion, and continuity in (3) give a nonempty compact feasible set and an attained minimum.  The displayed slack hypothesis yields
\[
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}S_{B^\circ}(\xi_0)\right)\ge\kappa+\eta,
\]
so continuity of (1) makes the fixed basis \(B^\circ\) feasible for every sufficiently large \(j\).  Optimality and (3) then give
\[
w_{\xi_j}(B_j)\le w_{\xi_j}(B^\circ)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
w_{\xi_0}(B)\le w_{\xi_0}(B^\circ)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0).
\]
Feasibility of \(B\) supplies the reverse inequality, so \(B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\).  The same argument, with the optimization inequality reversed and \(g_{B,\xi}(0)\) in place of \(w_\xi(B)\), proves that every limit of a sequence \(B_j\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).

For every \(\xi\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\), ass:kappa-feasibility makes \(K(\xi)\) nonempty, prop:kappa-exhaustion makes it compact, and (3) makes both objectives continuous.  Thus both optimizer sets are nonempty and compact.  Define
\[
\phi_0(\xi)=\min_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_\xi(B),
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)=\max_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_\xi(B).
\]
Take a subsequence realizing \(\liminf_j\phi_0(\xi_j)\), select a minimizer from each \(\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)\), and then take a convergent further subsequence in the compact ambient quotient.  Sequential upper stability and (3) imply
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\phi_0(\xi_j)\ge\phi_0(\xi_0).
\tag{4}
\]
Applying the analogous argument to a subsequence realizing the upper limit and to maximizers over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)\) gives
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}\phi_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)
\le\phi_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0).
\tag{5}
\]
By def:dominance-gap, \(\Delta=\phi_0-\phi_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  Combining (4) and (5),
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)
\ge
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\phi_0(\xi_j)
-\limsup_{j\to\infty}\phi_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)
\ge\Delta(\xi_0),
\]
as claimed. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact design and endpoint inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized representatives \(B(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}x&0\\0&y\end{bmatrix}\), the full optimizer correspondences are
\[
\mathcal A_0=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=\mathbf 1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,\ 
(\mathbf 1^{\top}y)^2=\frac{216}{55}
\right\}.
\]
They are nonempty, and their exact objective values satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200}\quad(B_0\in\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}
\quad(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}).
\]
Moreover every member of \(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obeys
\[
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}.
\]
Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the rational choices
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the full-correspondence certificates
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)
-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=\delta>0
\]
and
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}
=\eta>0.
\]

\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U),
\]

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite network \(G\), known assignment law \(\nu\), known exposure maps \(f_i\), and two mutually exclusive exposure events.
sampling_model.units: The realized finite-population potential outcomes are fixed for design-based estimation; the i.i.d. law \(H\) is used only to choose the basis ex ante.
sampling_model.treatment: The main experiment draws \(W\sim\nu\), and assignment is the only randomness in the causal estimator conditional on the chosen basis.
sampling_model.overlap: Every exposure probability \(\pi_{i,a}\) is positive, and basis covariance is bounded below by \(\kappa\) on the optimization class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two arm-specific external or historical i.i.d. samples are mutually unpaired and independent of the later assignment; they estimate \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), while the cross-world copula is neither estimated nor assumed.

tldr: Rare network exposures make Horvitz--Thompson estimation noisy, and Zhao's optimal indicator control variates reduce this design variance, but the ex ante basis depends on a cross-world covariance that an unpaired pilot cannot identify. The contribution chain imports the sharp Fréchet covariance range, proves a new fixed-basis affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's objective, poses certified global maximin optimization on the fixed-\(\kappa\) projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency without assuming away ties. Neighborhood persistence is supporting and witness-gated; no strict-dominance region is claimed unless the full-correspondence separation-and-slack certificate is produced.

project_justification.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates explicitly leaves robust basis choice under moment misspecification open; existing Fréchet results identify covariance endpoints, and existing global-optimization results certify Euclidean-box programs, but no paper joins these steps for a block-separable network basis with projective symmetry.
project_justification.niche: Two unpaired pilot marginals identify the exact dependence ambiguity relevant to Zhao's moment matrix while leaving the experimental network and assignment law fixed and known.
project_justification.fill: The project imports the sharp endpoint formulas, proves their affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, formulates a computably specified global maximin certificate on the compact \(\kappa\)-regular projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency. Conditional persistence is supporting: a strict-dominance region requires a separate certified witness with both separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack.

technical_internal_limitation: The presolve fractions \(521/1200\), \(2613/8432\), and \(4912/39525\) are not formal claims because the triangle exposure truth tables, the resulting entries of \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), the value of \(\kappa\), full equality-set bounds, and optimizer-wide strict \(\kappa\)-slack certificate are not supplied. The early kill test is oeq:separated-lawful-witness over exact assignment enumeration and both full optimizer correspondences. Unnumbered sanity check and regression test: if \(F_1\) and \(F_0\) are point masses, then the definitions give \(c_L=c_U=0\), hence \(r(B)=g_B(0)\) and \(\mathcal A_R=\mathcal A_0\). Zhao's Corollary 3 supports the stronger noiseless inverse-probability-weighted basis special case, while this correspondence equality is only a definitional code check and carries no theorem or novelty status.
honest_scope: The sharp Fréchet covariance range is imported from AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1. The new theorem targets are its affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, projective compactness, uniform plug-in value and outer-set consistency, and conditional neighborhood persistence. The finite epsilon-global solver and the separated lawful witness are first-class open constructions. Persistence is incremental and yields a strict-dominance region only after the witness supplies both a positive full-correspondence separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack; no such region is otherwise claimed. No SDP reduction, universal minimax interchange, universal strict improvement, asymptotic normality for the pilot-selected basis, or point convergence under ties is claimed.
